problem_text:
A retail distribution center must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a seasonal beverage over an upcoming 18-week promotional window.  
The starting stock level at the commencement of this window is precisely zero cases.  
In each week \( t = 1,\dots,18 \), the beverage supplier permits the center to submit a procurement request, where the number of cases requested must be no fewer than 7 and no more than 56.  
Each procurement, once placed, requires 0 weeks of lead time before it becomes available to meet weekly requirements or to augment the stock.  
The projected weekly requirement for the beverage is detailed as follows:  
* Week 1: requirement 30 cases  
* Week 2: requirement 57 cases  
* Week 3: requirement 52 cases  
* Week 4: requirement 49 cases  
* Week 5: requirement 39 cases  
* Week 6: requirement 42 cases  
* Week 7: requirement 32 cases  
* Week 8: requirement 24 cases  
* Week 9: requirement 59 cases  
* Week 10: requirement 42 cases  
* Week 11: requirement 12 cases  
* Week 12: requirement 56 cases  
* Week 13: requirement 34 cases  
* Week 14: requirement 60 cases  
* Week 15: requirement 33 cases  
* Week 16: requirement 31 cases  
* Week 17: requirement 60 cases  
* Week 18: requirement 42 cases  

Stock‑outs are permissible; however, any weekly requirement that cannot be fulfilled from available stock is entirely forfeited and will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the 18‑week horizon, quantities of the beverage may be treated as continuous, and the total physical stock held in the warehouse at any moment must not surpass the facility’s capacity of 48 cases.  
The aggregate expense incurred over the planning window comprises three distinct elements: the procurement expense, charged at 4 per case ordered; the storage expense, levied at 1 per case held in stock from one week to the next; and a penalty for unmet requirement, assessed at 11 per case of forfeited weekly demand.  
The objective is to ascertain the optimal procurement quantity for each week and to monitor the consequent stock levels and weekly shortfalls, with the aim of minimizing the total expense.
